why: git accepts any UNAMBIGUOUS abbreviation of a long option, so `--no-veri` skips hooks/pre-commit exactly as completely as the full spelling — verified against git 2.50.1 with a pre-commit hook that exits 1: the commit lands. An equality test against the full string sees neither this nor `--no-verif`. `--no-ver` is deliberately NOT covered: it is ambiguous with `--no-verbose` and git refuses to run it, so denying it would refuse a command that cannot skip anything.
